title: Window and Door Rebates in Richmond 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: Richmond homes can claim $100 per window or door from BC Hydro, up to $2,000. 26% of households live in pre-1981 homes. Rules, an example and steps.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Richmond
lead: Richmond is flat, open and close to the water. Windows and doors face the wind more than in a sheltered neighbourhood, so a good seal matters here. The rebate pays $100 for each one you replace.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Richmond
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Richmond family house

Replacing 14 windows and 3 exterior doors is 17 openings, or $1,700. If you also have a sliding patio door, it is another opening. Past 20 openings the cap of $2,000 stops the rebate growing.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 81,080 households in Richmond. About 21,040 (26%) live in homes built before 1981, and 7,175 are owner-occupied detached houses from that era. Another 42% of households live in apartments, and 29% rent. About 71% of Richmond households own their home.

Richmond's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 1.5°C and the coldest day was -14.4°C. That is a mild record. Window savings on the heating bill are modest, so most of the benefit shows up as fewer drafts and less condensation.

The rebate pays for exterior doors that replace existing ones between a heated space and the outdoors or an unheated space. A front door, back door or patio door counts as one opening each. Interior doors do not. A door must meet the same U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, so a plain hollow door will not qualify.

• Installed by a licensed contractor with a GST number and a BC business licence. Self-installation is not eligible.
  • Units must be new and not previously installed elsewhere.
  • The home must be at least 12 months old.
  • Apply within six months of the invoice date, with the invoice and label photos.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

You have six months from the invoice date to apply, and the application needs the invoice and a photo of the manufacturer label on each unit. BC Hydro publishes a window and door checklist and a sample invoice. Ask the contractor to fill in the invoice the way the sample does, listing each window or door separately. A vague invoice is the usual reason a claim is sent back.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Check the home is electric-heated and at least 12 months old.
Get quotes that list the U-factor of each window and door.
Photograph each label on installation day.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation or a water heater to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: Yes. Exterior doors that replace existing ones between heated and unheated space count as one opening each.
